3. The learned Senior Advocate Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmood next further taken his 2nd bench of gourd and argues that the instant suit is hopelessly barred by the law of limitation since the plaintiff failed to institute the suit within 2(two) years from the alleged date of cause of action and contends that for these two reason as the suit is barred by law, the same comes under the perview of Order 7 Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and as such the plaint is liable to be rejected. 

 5. The instant application under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 read with section 151 reveals that the prayer for rejection of the plaint rests upon two grounds mainly the 'Barge' out of which the cause of action of the suit has arisen is not at all a vessel so as to institute suit in the Admiralty Jurisdiction and further that the instant suit is barred by law of limitation. 

 10. Therefore, a duty is cast upon this Court to examine whether the suit comes under the purview of the Admiralty Jurisdiction or not and whether the same is barred under the law of limitation. 

 24. In his second bunch of argument the learned Senior Advocate Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmood, submits that the cause of action of the plaintiff arises when the plaintiff failed to remove the Barges from where it has been put for use as a causeway and that being two years ago the suit is barred by limitation under the Provisions of Article 137 of the Limitation Act. 

 25. On the other hand the learned Advocate Mr. Tanjibul Alam argued that the question of limitation is a mixed question of law and fact and unless the evidence is taken regarding when and how the limitation has started or ended no decision on the point of limitation can be taken. 

 26. We are in agreement with the learned Advocate Mr. Tanjibul Alam. The question of limitation is hybrid question of law and fact and question whether the suit is barred by limitation can only be decided upon getting evidence on the point and as such the plaint cannot be rejected on the ground of limitation under the inherent jurisdiction of this court unless the ground of limitation is apparent on the face of the plaint.
